livePriceFeeds.description: How the client fetches live asset prices and what the backend should be aware of for server-side valuation.

crypto.plan: Free public tier — no API key required
crypto.calledFrom: Client-side only (browser fetch) — NOT proxied through the Celerey backend

clientCaching.strategy: On load, check cache first. If cache is fresh AND all active crypto holdings are covered, use cache. Otherwise fetch fresh from CoinGecko. User can also force-refresh manually.

crypto.rateLimitNote: CoinGecko free tier allows ~30 req/min. The client batches all crypto symbols into a single request per fetch cycle, so this is not a concern at current scale. If Celerey scales to many concurrent users, move the fetch to the backend and cache server-side.
crypto.fallback: If the fetch fails or times out (8s timeout), the client falls back silently to the stored current_value on the holding record — the UI does not crash.

stocks_etfs_bonds.status: No live feed implemented yet — uses manual / stored current_value from the holding record
stocks_etfs_bonds.backendNote: When you add stock/ETF live prices, the fetch should go through the Celerey backend (not directly from the client) so the API key stays secret. The backend can then cache per-symbol prices in Redis with a 15-min TTL and return current_value in the AssetHolding response.

backendValuationResponsibility.description: When the backend returns AssetHolding objects, it should populate current_value based on valuation_method:
backendValuationResponsibility.market: Fetch live price from the relevant provider (CoinGecko for crypto; Finnhub/Twelve Data for stocks/ETFs). current_value = quantity * live_price.
backendValuationResponsibility.auto_calculated: Compute accrued value server-side. For bonds: current_value = cost_basis * (1 + coupon_rate/100)^years_held. For cash: similar compound interest logic.
backendValuationResponsibility.manual: Return the current_value as stored — no computation. The last_updated timestamp tells the client when it was last manually updated.

endpoints.description: Get the user's retirement config and computed projections

config.desiredMonthlyIncome: number — target monthly income in retirement

notes: projections are computed server-side using the standard retirement formula: FV = PV*(1+r)^n + PMT*((1+r)^n - 1)/r
sustainableAnnualIncome = projectedBalance * safeWithdrawalRatePct / 100
inflationAdjustedSustainableMonthlyIncome discounts by inflationPct over yearsToRetirement

crossTabRelationships.description: When user_type = 'enterprise' the client skips /choose-plan entirely and gets full feature access. The client reads user_type from localStorage as soon as the user logs in.
Saving a risk assessment updates user.risk_profile synchronously. Profile and Settings pages read risk_profile from the User object.

System scenarios are shown in a selector on the Goals page. The selected scenario adjusts the displayed monthlyContributionNeeded: adjustedMonthly = goal.monthlyContributionNeeded / ((1 + scenario.monthlyReturnRate) / (1 + scenario.inflationRate / 12))
The retirement goal card reads retirement.projections.onTrack and sustainableMonthlyIncome to display alongside user-created goals
